Tina — thanks for the manifest. High-level confirmation below; attaching our proposed acceptance checklist and signed image token (signed_image_20261011.sig).

Summary of proposed flow (short):
1) Courier delivers sealed media to Acme cold-room. Acme ops verifies external tamper-evidence and signs physical receipt.
2) Operator opens sealed tamper bag in presence of Acme witness and Redwood remote observer (we join via low-bandwidth video feed).
3) Acme provides operator-signed acceptance record; Redwood verifies the image signature (signed_image_20261011.sig) against our public key repository. Remote pre-check verifies manifest hashes (we do not transfer image over network).
4) Activation window: we recommend a 2-hour activation slot during which the operator performs installation and a 60-minute smoke test.
5) Rollforward authorization: if the smoke test passes and signatures match, Acme ops confirms activation with a signed ACK. If a post-activation integrity issue is discovered, emergency revocation is initiated by Acme security and Redwood will automatically block further activations and provide forensic artifacts.

Key clarifications you asked for:
- Remote signature verification: yes — Redwood will perform verification of the image signature and manifest hashes when you provide the manifest and signature file over an encrypted channel (SFTP or signed link). We will respond with a signed verification token within 30 minutes of successful verification.
- Operator presence: Redwood requires an Acme operator to perform the physical handoff and initial install; Redwood remote observer suffices for signature verification and acceptance.
- Emergency revocation contact: Kimberly Park (kimberly_park@redwood.com) and our security lead Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwood.com).

Attachments: coldroom_deployment_plan_v1.pdf (application/pdf), signed_image_20261011.sig (application/octet-stream)

Next steps: I've attached a one-page acceptance checklist; if you can approve by EOD Wednesday we'll schedule the remote verification window and DocuSign the MOA.

—

Marissa — this is mostly what our security doc requires, thanks. A couple items we need clarified before signoff:

1) Verification token handling: Can Redwood provide a short-lived signed verification artifact that we can store alongside the courier manifest? We want a timestamped token (ISO + signature) that attests to the verification result for our audit trail.
2) Rollback authorization granularity: If the operator finds a non-critical integrity warning during the 60-minute smoke test (for example, a missing non-essential label), who within Redwood can authorize a rollforward vs require quarantine? We need a delegated list.
3) If the image signature fails, do you provide a forensic package and timeline for turnaround on root-cause? Our legal team wants an SLA for forensic response.

If you can add those answers to the MOA we can route to SOC for the Wednesday deadline.

—Rajiv
Engineering Lead, Deployment Services
Acme Pharma
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Rajiv — thanks, responses inline and updated language we'll put into the MOA (see excerpt below). We'll attach the updated one-page MOA to the DocuSign link and share the verification token format example in Drive.

Inline answers:
1) Verification token: yes — Redwood will produce a short-lived JSON verification token (timestamp ISO8601, manifest_hash, verification_result, signer_id) signed with our key. Example stored on Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1abcColdRoomPlan. Token TTL will be 24 hours by default; we can extend per request. We will also store a copy in our audit logs for 1 year and provide exports on request.

2) Rollforward delegation: If a non-critical warning appears during the smoke test, the following Redwood delegates can authorize rollforward after a brief engineering triage (<= 45 minutes):
- Kimberly Park — Product Security Manager (kimberly_park@redwood.com)
- Priyom Das — Field Ops Lead (priyom_das@redwood.com)
- Marissa Cole — Solutions Lead (marissa_cole@redwood.com)

Critical failures (signature mismatch, corrupted artifact) automatically trigger quarantine and forensic intake; rollforward is not permitted.

3) Forensic SLA: Redwood will deliver an initial forensic package (hashes, verification logs, signature chain) within 8 business hours and an initial root-cause summary within 3 business days. We'll prioritize hotfix artifacts if needed.

MOA excerpt we'll add: 
- "Redwood provides signed verification token (TTL 24h) on successful manifest and signature verification; token stored in both parties' audit logs'"
- "Rollforward is permitted only after delegation confirmation from a named Redwood delegate; critical failures require quarantine and forensics."
- "Forensic response: initial package within 8 business hours, root-cause summary within 3 business days."

Action items:
- I'll upload the MOA to DocuSign and share the link before 11:30am PT Thursday.
- Kimberly / Priyom: please confirm you can act as delegates for the Oct 20 window (reply-all).
- Tina / Rajiv: if that SLA cadence is acceptable, reply with a quick ACK and we'll proceed to DocuSign.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

—
